guard: a message wait matches the principal the broker bound to the message, never the payload's display name
why: The suite imports the runtime source directly, so no rebuild is needed for these mutations.
Two checks, mutated apart because each guards a case the other does not reach. The from.id
check is the only guard when the wait has no `from`, and the only guard against a post on the
seat's own subject that names someone else. The sender comparison is the only guard against
another principal posting under the seat's name, on a message that is otherwise authentic.
The third mutation removes the roster resolution, which leaves the wait with no sender to
compare, so the impostor answers again.

mutations.name: the from.id check is dropped, so a message whose payload names another sender than its subject can answer
mutations.expectRed: a post on the seat's own subject carrying a different from.id is ignored
mutations.cell: a post on the seat's own subject carrying a different from.id is ignored

mutations.name: the sender comparison is dropped, so any principal on the channel answers a wait with `from`
mutations.find: if (sender !== undefined && parsed.sender !== sender) return false;
mutations.expectRed: impostors posting APPROVED from their own principals
mutations.cell: impostors posting APPROVED from their own principals

mutations.name: the `from` handle is never resolved through the roster, so the wait has no sender to match
mutations.find: const sender = ev.event === "message" && ev.from !== undefined ? this.waitSender(ev.from) : undefined;
mutations.replace: const sender = undefined as string | undefined;
mutations.expectRed: impostors posting APPROVED from their own principals
mutations.cell: impostors posting APPROVED from their own principals
